newsitem.title: INDIA: India Chidambaram says inflation down at 5.93 pct.
newsitem.headline: India Chidambaram says inflation down at 5.93 pct.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday that inflation rate, measured by the wholesale price index, was down to 5.93 percent in the latest week compared with 6.0 percent in the previous week.
"Macroeconomic indices have never been better," Chidambaram told an advertising awards function.
The industrial output had the potential to grow about 10 percent in the current fiscal year, 1997/98 (April/March), he said.

Last week the government reported that industrial output -- a key barometer for the overall economy -- inched up by only 2.4 percent in February over the same month in 1996. The growth rate in February 1996 was a blistering 13.3 percent.
Between April 1996 and February 1997 -- the first 11 months of the last fiscal year -- industrial production expanded by seven percent, down from 11.8 percent in the same period in 1995/96.
Chidambaram said bank deposits had increased by 100.8 billion rupees ($2.8 billion) since the start of the financial year on April 1.
"Now is the time for industry to go to the capital markets to raise money for investments," he said.
He said foreign investors' confidence in India was manifest in a foreign exchange inflow into the country at the rate of $300 million each week. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
